Project Area 01

Cal Poly Space Systems

On the Booster Team at Cal Poly Space Systems, I've worked across aerodynamic structures, flight hardware, manufacturing, assembly, and test preparation. I currently co-lead the center-stage separation work for a full shuttle configuration with two side boosters and a center stage.

Sub-Section

Booster and Center Stage Projects

Booster Separation Mechanism

Team Lead Test Jig Mechanism Design

As Center Stage Team Lead, I am leading research and concept development for the booster separation mechanism. My team is evaluating multiple approaches, including an explosive pin concept, explosive bolt testing, and an electromagnetic system. I am currently overseeing 3D-printed test models and a jig-and-pin setup used to study separation angle and required separation force before final mechanism manufacturing.

Airfoil

SolidWorks DevFoam Mach3

I modeled the airfoil's aerodynamic surface in SolidWorks, then converted the 3D geometry into 2D toolpaths ready for manufacturing. Using DevFoam and Mach3, I generated and checked the G-code for CNC hot-wire foam cutting, dialing in feed rate, wire temperature, and axis alignment so the finished piece kept its intended airfoil shape.

Canard and Vertical Stabilizer Wings

Airfoil Design Hot-Wire Cutting Manufacturing

I designed and built the booster's wing canards, shaping custom airfoil profiles around the manufacturing constraints we were working with. To cut them, I also built a manual hot-wire cutting rig with a rigid, aligned frame, accounting for heat transfer through the wire to get clean cuts without burning through or weakening the foam.

Booster Assembly

Fiberglass Layups Assembly Flight Hardware

I helped manufacture and assemble the booster end to end: cutting foam components, integrating the canards, vertical stabilizer, fuselage sections, and nose cone, and laying up multiple fiberglass coats over the structure. From there I supported finishing work: Bondo, sanding, painting, motor assembly, wiring, actuator troubleshooting, launch prep, and reviewing what happened after each flight.

Servo Housing

SolidWorks 3D Printing

I designed a servo housing in SolidWorks to precisely align servo motors with the airfoil flaps, iterating through 3+ printed versions to get the fitment and electronic alignment right. Mounted inside the fuselage at the center of the booster, this housing let the airfoil flaps actuate correctly in flight.
